title: Vision Transformers (ViT)
description: Vision Transformers (ViT): Apply Transformers to images! Revolutionary: No convolutions needed. Architecture: (1) Split image into patches (16×16). (2) Flatten patches → linear projection → embeddings. (3) Add positional embeddings. (4) Standard Transformer encoder (multi-head attention, MLP). (5) Classification head on [CLS] token. Key insight: Image = sequence of patches! Each patch = token (like word in NLP). Self-attention learns spatial relationships. Advantages: (1) Global receptive field (vs CNN's local). (2) Better scaling with data. (3) Transfer learning from large datasets. Challenges: Needs large datasets (ImageNet-21k). Patch size trade-off: Smaller → more tokens → higher compute. Models: ViT-Base, ViT-Large, ViT-Huge. Hybrid: CNN stem + Transformer. Applications: Image classification, object detection (DETR), segmentation. State-of-the-art on ImageNet with sufficient data.

content.level0_basic: Vision Transformers (ViT): Use Transformer (NLP architecture) for images! How: (1) Cut image into patches (like puzzle pieces). 16×16 pixels each. (2) Each patch = token (like word!). (3) Flatten patch, make embedding. (4) Feed to Transformer! Self-attention between patches. (5) Classification token [CLS] → predict class. Why revolutionary? CNN: Local filters (3×3, 5×5), hierarchical. ViT: Global attention from layer 1! Every patch can attend to every other. Better understanding of relationships. Example: 224×224 image → 14×14 patches (196 tokens). Transformer processes all 196 simultaneously! Challenge: Needs LOTS of data. CNNs work with small datasets, ViT needs millions. Solution: Pre-train on huge dataset (ImageNet-21k), then fine-tune. Results: Beats CNNs when data sufficient! Less inductive bias = more flexible.
content.level1_beginner:
**ViT Architecture:**

```
1. Image (224×224×3)
   ↓
2. Split into patches (16×16)
   → 196 patches (14×14 grid)
   ↓
3. Flatten each patch: 16×16×3 = 768
   ↓
4. Linear projection: 768 → d_model (768)
   ↓
5. Add positional embeddings
   + Add [CLS] token (classification)
   ↓
6. Transformer Encoder (12 layers)
   - Multi-head self-attention
   - MLP (feedforward)
   ↓
7. Take [CLS] token output
   ↓
8. Classification head: MLP → classes
```

**Patch Embedding:**

```
Image: H×W×3
Patch size: P×P
Number of patches: N = (H/P) × (W/P)

Each patch: P×P×3 = P²×3 dimensions
Flatten: Vector of size P²×3
Linear projection: P²×3 → d_model

Result: N × d_model token embeddings
Add: [CLS] token → (N+1) × d_model
```

**Positional Embeddings:**

```python
# Learnable positional embeddings
num_patches = 196  # 14×14
pos_embed = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, num_patches + 1, 768))

# Add to patch embeddings
x = patch_embeddings + pos_embed

# Why needed? Transformer doesn't know patch positions!
# Positional embeddings encode: "This patch is at position (i,j)"
```

**Self-Attention in ViT:**

```
Each patch attends to all other patches!

Patch 1 (top-left): Attends to patch 100 (bottom-right)
→ Can capture long-range dependencies

CNN: Receptive field grows slowly
  Layer 1: 3×3 local
  Layer 10: Still limited
  
ViT: Global receptive field from Layer 1!
  Every patch sees every other patch
  Better for understanding whole image
```

**ViT vs CNN:**

```
Inductive Bias:
  CNN: Strong (locality, translation equivariance)
  ViT: Weak (learns from data)
  
Data Requirement:
  CNN: Works with small datasets (10k images)
  ViT: Needs large datasets (millions)
  
Performance:
  Small data: CNN wins
  Large data: ViT wins!
  
Computational Cost:
  CNN: O(H·W·C²·k²) (kernel size k)
  ViT: O(N²·d) (N patches, attention O(N²))
```
content.level2_application:
**ViT Implementation:**

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class PatchEmbedding(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, img_size=224, patch_size=16, in_channels=3, embed_dim=768):
        super().__init__()
        self.num_patches = (img_size // patch_size) ** 2
        
        # Convolution does patching + projection!
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(
            in_channels, embed_dim,
            kernel_size=patch_size,
            stride=patch_size
        )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        # x: (B, 3, 224, 224)
        x = self.proj(x)  # (B, 768, 14, 14)
        x = x.flatten(2)  # (B, 768, 196)
        x = x.transpose(1, 2)  # (B, 196, 768)
        return x

class VisionTransformer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, img_size=224, patch_size=16, num_classes=1000,
                 embed_dim=768, depth=12, num_heads=12):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Patch embedding
        self.patch_embed = PatchEmbedding(img_size, patch_size, 3, embed_dim)
        num_patches = (img_size // patch_size) ** 2
        
        # [CLS] token
        self.cls_token = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, 1, embed_dim))
        
        # Positional embeddings
        self.pos_embed = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, num_patches + 1, embed_dim))
        
        # Transformer encoder
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=embed_dim,
            nhead=num_heads,
            dim_feedforward=embed_dim * 4,
            dropout=0.1
        )
        self.transformer = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, depth)
        
        # Classification head
        self.head = nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_classes)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        B = x.shape[0]
        
        # Patch embedding
        x = self.patch_embed(x)  # (B, 196, 768)
        
        # Add [CLS] token
        cls_tokens = self.cls_token.expand(B, -1, -1)
        x = torch.cat([cls_tokens, x], dim=1)  # (B, 197, 768)
        
        # Add positional embedding
        x = x + self.pos_embed
        
        # Transformer
        x = self.transformer(x)
        
        # Classification: Use [CLS] token
        cls_output = x[:, 0]
        logits = self.head(cls_output)
        
        return logits

# Create model
model = VisionTransformer(
    img_size=224,
    patch_size=16,
    num_classes=1000,
    embed_dim=768,
    depth=12,
    num_heads=12
)

print(f'Parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())/1e6:.1f}M')
```

**ViT with Hybrid Architecture:**

```python
class HybridViT(nn.Module):
    """CNN stem + Transformer"""
    def __init__(self, num_classes=1000):
        super().__init__()
        
        # ResNet stem (initial layers)
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 7, stride=2, padding=3),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(3, stride=2, padding=1),
            # ResNet blocks...
        )
        
        # Flatten CNN features as patches
        self.patch_embed = nn.Conv2d(64, 768, kernel_size=1)
        
        # Transformer (same as ViT)
        self.transformer = TransformerEncoder(...)
        self.head = nn.Linear(768, num_classes)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        # CNN feature extraction
        x = self.stem(x)  # (B, 64, H', W')
        
        # Treat as patches
        x = self.patch_embed(x)  # (B, 768, H', W')
        x = x.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
        
        # Transformer
        x = self.transformer(x)
        return self.head(x[:, 0])
```

**Attention Visualization:**

```python
@torch.no_grad()
def visualize_attention(model, image):
    """Visualize what patches attend to"""
    model.eval()
    
    # Forward with attention weights
    attentions = []
    hooks = []
    
    def hook_fn(module, input, output):
        attentions.append(output[1])  # Attention weights
    
    # Register hooks on attention layers
    for layer in model.transformer.layers:
        hooks.append(layer.self_attn.register_forward_hook(hook_fn))
    
    output = model(image)
    
    # Remove hooks
    for hook in hooks:
        hook.remove()
    
    # Visualize attention from [CLS] to patches
    cls_attention = attentions[-1][0, :, 0, 1:]  # Last layer, [CLS] to patches
    
    # Reshape to image
    num_patches = int(cls_attention.shape[-1] ** 0.5)
    attention_map = cls_attention.reshape(num_patches, num_patches)
    
    return attention_map
```

**DETR: Detection Transformer:**

```python
class DETR(nn.Module):
    """Object detection with ViT"""
    def __init__(self, num_classes=91):
        super().__init__()
        
        # CNN backbone
        self.backbone = resnet50()
        
        # Transformer encoder-decoder
        self.transformer = nn.Transformer(
            d_model=256, nhead=8,
            num_encoder_layers=6,
            num_decoder_layers=6
        )
        
        # Object queries (learnable)
        self.query_embed = nn.Embedding(100, 256)  # 100 objects max
        
        # Prediction heads
        self.class_head = nn.Linear(256, num_classes + 1)  # +1 for 'no object'
        self.bbox_head = nn.Linear(256, 4)  # x, y, w, h
    
    def forward(self, x):
        # Extract features
        features = self.backbone(x)
        
        # Transformer
        h = self.transformer(
            features.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2),
            self.query_embed.weight.unsqueeze(1)
        )
        
        # Predictions
        classes = self.class_head(h)
        boxes = self.bbox_head(h).sigmoid()
        
        return {'pred_logits': classes, 'pred_boxes': boxes}
```

whatIsIt: Vision Transformers (ViT): Apply Transformer architecture to computer vision! Key idea: Image = sequence of patches. Architecture: (1) Split image into patches (16×16 pixels). (2) Flatten and linearly project patches → embeddings. (3) Add learnable positional embeddings (encode spatial positions). (4) Prepend [CLS] token for classification. (5) Standard Transformer encoder (multi-head self-attention + MLP). (6) Classification head on [CLS] output. Attention mechanism: Each patch attends to all other patches → global receptive field from layer 1! No convolutions needed. Models: ViT-Base/16 (86M params), ViT-Large/16 (307M), ViT-Huge/14 (632M). Training: Requires large datasets (ImageNet-21k: 14M images). Transfer learning: Pre-train on large dataset, fine-tune on target task.
whyNeeded: Why ViT vs CNN? (1) Global Receptive Field: CNNs have local filters, receptive field grows slowly. ViT: Every patch sees every other patch from layer 1 → better understanding of whole image. (2) Scaling: CNNs saturate with more data. ViT: Performance keeps improving with larger datasets! Less inductive bias → learns more from data. (3) Transfer Learning: Pre-train once on huge dataset, transfer to many tasks (classification, detection, segmentation). (4) Unified Architecture: Same Transformer for NLP + Vision → potential for multimodal models (CLIP, GPT-4V). Challenges: (1) Data hungry: Needs millions of images. CNNs work with thousands. (2) Compute intensive: Attention O(N²) in patch count. Solutions: Hybrid models (CNN stem + Transformer), efficient attention variants. State-of-the-art: ViT beats ResNet when data sufficient! Modern era: Transformers everywhere.
realWorldAnalogy: ViT = Puzzle solving strategy! CNN approach: Look at pieces locally. Start corner, gradually expand. Local patterns first, big picture later. ViT approach: Look at ALL pieces simultaneously! See entire puzzle at once. Find relationships: 'This piece (patch 1) relates to that distant piece (patch 100) because colors match'. Global understanding from start. Patch = Puzzle piece. Self-attention = 'Which pieces relate to which?' [CLS] token = Final answer: 'It's a cat!' Why better (with enough pieces/data)? Global view helps! CNN might miss long-range relationships. ViT sees everything. Why harder? Need MANY puzzles to learn (data requirement). Without experience (inductive bias), need lots of examples. CNN: Born knowing 'nearby pieces usually connect' (locality bias). ViT: Learns everything from scratch → needs more data but more flexible!

formulas: \text{Patches: } N = \frac{H \cdot W}{P^2}, \quad \text{where } P \text{ is patch size}

stepByStep: 2. Split into patches: N = (H/P)×(W/P) patches of size P×P
3. Flatten each patch: P²×3 dimensional vectors
4. Linear projection: Map to d_model dimensions
a. Multi-head self-attention (patches attend to each other)
9. Classification head: Linear layer → class logits
algorithm.complexity: Patch embedding: O(H·W·C·d). Transformer: O(L·N²·d + L·N·d²) where L=layers, N=patches, d=dimension. Attention: O(N²·d) per layer (quadratic in patches!). For 224×224 image, 16×16 patches: N=196. ViT-Base (L=12): ~86M parameters. Inference: ~10-30ms on GPU.

codeExamples.title: Complete ViT Model
codeExamples.code:
class VisionTransformer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, img_size=224, patch_size=16, num_classes=1000, embed_dim=768, depth=12, num_heads=12):
        super().__init__()
        num_patches = (img_size // patch_size) ** 2
        
        self.patch_embed = nn.Conv2d(3, embed_dim, patch_size, stride=patch_size)
        self.cls_token = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, 1, embed_dim))
        self.pos_embed = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, num_patches + 1, embed_dim))
        
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(embed_dim, num_heads, embed_dim*4, 0.1)
        self.transformer = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, depth)
        self.head = nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_classes)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        B = x.shape[0]
        x = self.patch_embed(x).flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
        cls_tokens = self.cls_token.expand(B, -1, -1)
        x = torch.cat([cls_tokens, x], dim=1)
        x = x + self.pos_embed
        x = self.transformer(x)
        return self.head(x[:, 0])

model = VisionTransformer()
print(f'{sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())/1e6:.1f}M params')

codeExamples.code:
from transformers import ViTForImageClassification
import torch.nn as nn

# Load pre-trained ViT
model = ViTForImageClassification.from_pretrained(
    'google/vit-base-patch16-224',
    num_labels=10,  # Your dataset classes
    ignore_mismatched_sizes=True
)

# Freeze backbone, train only classifier
for param in model.vit.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False
for param in model.classifier.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = True

# Training
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.classifier.parameters(), lr=1e-3)

for images, labels in train_loader:
    outputs = model(images)
    loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()(outputs.logits, labels)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    optimizer.zero_grad()

print('Fine-tuning complete!')

class HybridViT(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes=1000):
        super().__init__()
        # CNN stem
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 7, stride=2, padding=3),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(3, stride=2, padding=1),
        )
        # Transformer
        self.transformer = nn.TransformerEncoder(
            nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(64, 4, 256),
            num_layers=6
        )
        self.head = nn.Linear(64, num_classes)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.stem(x)  # CNN features
        B, C, H, W = x.shape
        x = x.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)  # (B, H*W, C)
        x = self.transformer(x)
        return self.head(x.mean(1))  # Global average pooling

model = HybridViT()

quiz.question: ViT'de image patches'e neden dönüştürülür?
options: Transformer sequence of tokens bekler! Image → patches → tokens
quiz.explanation: Transformer architecture sequence of tokens için tasarlandı (NLP: words). ViT: Image → patches → treat as tokens! Each 16×16 patch = one token. Image (224×224) → 196 patches (14×14 grid). Self-attention: Patches attend to each other (like words in sentence). Without patching: Pixel-level attention O(H²W²) → too expensive! Patches reduce sequence length, make feasible.

quiz.question: ViT'nin CNN'e göre en büyük avantajı?
options: Global receptive field from layer 1: Every patch sees all patches!
quiz.explanation: ViT: Global receptive field immediately! Self-attention: Each patch attends to ALL other patches from first layer. CNN: Local receptive field (3×3, 5×5), grows slowly through layers. Layer 1: 3×3. Layer 10: Still limited. ViT: Better for understanding relationships across image. Example: Object in top-left relates to object in bottom-right → ViT captures easily. Why matters: Long-range dependencies, global context. Trade-off: Needs more data to learn (less inductive bias).

quiz.question: ViT neden büyük dataset gerektirir?
options: Weak inductive bias: Learns spatial structure from data, needs examples!
quiz.explanation: Inductive Bias: Prior knowledge built into architecture. CNN: Strong bias (locality, translation equivariance). Knows 'nearby pixels related'. ViT: Weak bias. Doesn't assume spatial structure! Must learn from data. Result: CNN works with 10k images. ViT needs 1M+. With sufficient data: ViT outperforms CNN (more flexible). Small data: CNN wins (built-in knowledge helps). Solution: Pre-train ViT on ImageNet-21k (14M images), then fine-tune!

quiz.question: [CLS] token'ın rolü nedir?
options: Aggregates information from all patches for classification
quiz.explanation: [CLS] token: Special token prepended to sequence (from BERT). Purpose: Global representation! Attends to all patches, aggregates information. Final layer: [CLS] output → classification head → class prediction. Alternative: Could use average of all patches. [CLS] advantages: Learned aggregation (better than simple average). During attention: [CLS] attends to important patches, ignores noise. Visualization: [CLS] attention shows which patches are important for classification!

quiz.question: ViT'de positional embeddings neden gerekli?
options: Transformer permutation-invariant! Pos embeddings encode patch positions
quiz.explanation: Transformer: Permutation-invariant! Without positional info: Same output for shuffled input. Problem for images: Spatial structure critical! Top-left ≠ bottom-right. Solution: Positional embeddings! Learnable vectors added to patch embeddings. Encode: 'This patch is at position (i,j)'. Two types: Absolute (learned per position) or relative (distances). ViT: Uses learnable absolute. Result: Model knows spatial relationships!

quiz.question: Hybrid ViT (CNN + Transformer) neden kullanılır?
options: Best of both: CNN inductive bias + Transformer global attention
quiz.explanation: Hybrid: CNN stem (early layers) + Transformer (later layers). Benefits: (1) CNN: Low-level features (edges, textures) with inductive bias. (2) Transformer: High-level relationships with global attention. (3) Smaller dataset requirement than pure ViT. (4) Often better performance/data trade-off. Example: ResNet50 backbone → Transformer on top. CNN extracts feature map → treat as patches → Transformer processes. Popular: Combines strengths of both architectures!

commonMistakes.mistake: Using ViT on small datasets without pre-training
commonMistakes.why: ViT needs millions of images to learn spatial structure! On small datasets (10k images): Severe underfitting, poor performance. CNN will dominate.
commonMistakes.fix: Always pre-train ViT on large dataset (ImageNet-21k: 14M images), then fine-tune! Or use hybrid CNN+Transformer (better inductive bias). For small datasets: Stick with CNN or use heavy data augmentation with ViT. Rule: <100k images → CNN or pre-trained ViT only.

commonMistakes.why: Transformer is permutation-invariant! Without positional embeddings: Model can't distinguish patch locations. Shuffled image → same output. Spatial structure lost!
commonMistakes.fix: Always add positional embeddings! Either: (1) Learnable absolute positions (standard ViT), or (2) Sinusoidal (like original Transformer), or (3) Relative position bias. Critical for maintaining spatial information. Without it: Model sees patches as unordered set, not grid!

commonMistakes.why: Too small patches (4×4): Too many tokens (3136 for 224×224) → O(N²) attention explodes! Too large (32×32): Too few tokens (49) → lose spatial resolution.
commonMistakes.fix: Standard patch sizes: 16×16 (196 tokens, good balance) or 14×14 (256 tokens, slightly better). For high-res images (384×384): Can use 16×16 (576 tokens). Rule: N=196-1024 patches typical. Balance: Spatial resolution vs computational cost. ViT-Base/16 = 16×16 patches standard.

commonMistakes.why: ViT has weak inductive bias → prone to overfitting! Without augmentation: Memorizes training set. Poor generalization.
commonMistakes.fix: Use aggressive augmentation! RandAugment, Mixup, CutMix, random erasing. ViT needs MORE augmentation than CNN! Also: Dropout (0.1), stochastic depth (drop layers randomly). Regularization critical for ViT. Pre-training on large dataset also acts as regularization.

commonMistakes.why: Self-attention: O(N²·d). 196 patches: 38k interactions per layer! 12 layers: Adds up. Larger images/smaller patches: Explodes quickly.
commonMistakes.fix: Be aware of compute! For high resolution: Use hierarchical approaches (Swin Transformer), efficient attention (linear variants), or hybrid models (CNN reduces spatial size first). Monitor: GPU memory, inference time. Pure ViT: Best for standard resolution (224×224). High-res: Need efficient variants.

commonMistakes.why: ViT training dynamics different from CNN! Wrong LR → divergence or slow convergence. Transformers sensitive to LR.
commonMistakes.fix: Use proper LR schedule! Warm-up: Start low (1e-7), increase to peak (1e-3) over 10k steps. Then: Cosine decay. For fine-tuning: Lower LR (1e-5 to 1e-4). Optimizer: Adam or AdamW (weight decay important!). ViT needs careful tuning, not same as CNN training!

commonMistakes.why: Fine-tuning all parameters on small dataset → overfitting! ViT is large (86M+ params). Full fine-tuning needs lots of data.
commonMistakes.fix: Freeze backbone, train only classifier head! Or: Gradual unfreezing (first classifier, then last few layers). For small datasets (<10k): Freeze all except head. Medium datasets (10-100k): Unfreeze last 3-6 layers. Large datasets (100k+): Full fine-tuning OK. Monitor validation loss carefully!
